title: An Erdős-Pósa theorem for cycles and faces of distinct lengths
summary: We show that for every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, every graph $G$ contains $k$ vertex-disjoint cycles of different lengths, or there exists a set $X \subseteq V(G)$ with $|X| \in \mathcal{O}(k^6\mathsf{polylog}(k))$ such that $G-X$ has at most $k-1$ cycle lengths. We also prove analogous results for facial lengths of embedded graphs. Let $G$ be a graph with a closed 2-cell embedding $ψ$ on a surface $Σ$ of Euler genus $g$, let $c$ be a colouring of the faces $\mathcal{F}(ψ)$ of $ψ$, and let $R(G,ψ)$ be the radial graph of $(G, ψ)$.
